A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Identifiable Latent Bandits work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v5 reports original synthetic and ADCB experiments, including model-fitting results, sequential-decision regret, and supplementary robustness analyses.

after.justification: v6 retains the original synthetic and ADCB experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains mean-contrastive feature learning, OLS reward fitting, and the same CPG, FPG, and FPG-TS procedures. The population formulation of Equation (5) and broader identifying assumptions revise the theoretical treatment without documenting a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Synthetic and ADCB environments, the contextual-bandit example, and the existing noise, distribution-shift, nonlinear-reward, and action-count scenarios are retained. The broader theoretical dimensionality assumption is not accompanied by new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets, including MAB, MAB Prior, LinUCB, VAE-based variants, regression, and oracle variants. The new comparison with Hong et al. (2020) concerns theoretical settings and bounds, not an additional experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, model depths, training settings, horizons, and experimental perturbations are unchanged. Clarified captions about refitting models and varying reward noise describe procedures already documented in v5.

E4.justification: The noise, distribution-shift, Age-removal, nonlinear-reward, action-count, and contextual-bandit analyses are retained. The action-count analysis moves from v5 Appendix E.6 to v6 Section 4; the new bias diagram illustrates theory rather than a new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten training seeds and standard-error bars based on the same 200 or 1000 seeds in corresponding experiments. No new uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the corresponding appendix result tables retain their numerical entries: v5 Tables 3–4 become v6 Tables 4–5. Existing experimental plot graphics also match, and the reported empirical findings remain unchanged after relocation and renumbering.

T1.justification: Assumptions 3.1–3.2 expand from invertible emissions with n=d to injective emissions with n≤d, supported by a revised change-of-variables derivation in Appendix B. Theorem 3.5 and Appendix D replace the perfect-model-only regret analysis with an error-dependent bound covering imperfect models. v6 also corrects identifiability quantifiers, the log-prior term, and Gaussian likelihood algebra.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about learning identifiable continuous latent bandits from observational data and improving personalization under identifying conditions. The theoretical additions support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 expands the explanation of model misspecification, motivates reward-informed adaptation and exploration, and explicitly recommends FPG. v6 also removes v5 Appendix E.7's assertion that the theory already permits any symmetric exponential-family noise.

D1.justification: v6 adds a code-and-data availability statement announcing access to the full ILB implementation, experiment-reproduction code, and generated ADCB data. Appendix H's hyperparameters, hardware, and timing information remain unchanged; the external resources themselves were not inspected.

R1.justification: v6 adds references on proximal causal inference, identifiable representations, and injective mappings, plus an explicit comparison with Hong et al. (2020) in Appendix D and Table 3. It removes the Abbasi-Yadkori et al. (2011) reference while retaining the overall novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v6 makes targeted prose corrections and explanatory rewrites, removes placeholder running-header text, and moves the affine-invariance remark, action-count discussion, and impact statement into the main text. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. v5 Figures 6 and 11 move into the main text, and v6 adds the theoretical bias diagram in Figure 8 and the comparison table in Table 3. Existing experimental graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 corrects formal definitions and likelihood calculations, develops the treatment of injective emissions and imperfect models, and supplies code/data access information. These improve mathematical precision and reproducibility. The new regret guarantee remains conditional on an assumed uniform prediction-error bound, limiting the practical gain; the empirical evidence is unchanged.
